It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1916 and earlier in the [[Philippine Assembly]] from 1907 to 1916.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 20, 2020}} The district consists of the central municipalities of [[Barugo]], [[Burauen]], [[Capoocan]], [[Carigara]], [[Dagami, Leyte|Dagami]], [[Dulag, Leyte|Dulag]], [[Jaro, Leyte|Jaro]], [[Julita, Leyte|Julita]], [[La Paz, Leyte|La Paz]], [[MacArthur, Leyte|MacArthur]], [[Mayorga, Leyte|Mayorga]], [[Pastrana, Leyte|Pastrana]], [[Tabontabon]] and [[Tunga, Leyte|Tunga]] since its second restoration in 1987. It is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Lolita Javier]] of the [[Nationalist People's Coalition]] (NPC).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=April 20, 2020}} Until 1931, it consisted of southern municipalities of undivided Leyte: [[Bato, Leyte|Bato]], [[Hilongos]], [[Hindang]], [[Inopacan]], and [[Matalom]], and present-day [[Southern Leyte]] municipalities of [[San Juan, Southern Leyte|Cabalian]] (now San Juan), [[Libagon, Southern Leyte|Libagon]], [[Liloan, Southern Leyte|Liloan]], [[Maasin]], [[Macrohon]], [[Malitbog, Southern Leyte|Malitbog]], [[Pintuyan]], and [[Sogod, Southern Leyte|Sogod]]. Following the creation of the [[Leyte's 5th congressional district|fifth district]], [[Albuera]], [[Baybay]], and [[Ormoc]] were added from the [[Leyte's 1st congressional district|first district]], while the present-day Southern Leyte municipalities were redistricted to the [[Leyte's 3rd congressional district|third district]];{{cite PH act|chamber=Act|number=3788|url=http://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l5564 |title=An Act Reorganizing the Representative Districts of the Province of Leyte and Creating a Fifth District|date=December 2, 1930 |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate= May 6, 2020}} [[Kananga, Leyte|Kananga]] was later established out of Ormoc in 1950.{{Cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=542 |date=June 17, 1950 |title=An Act Creating the Municipality of Kananga in the Province of Leyte|url=https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/13016 |access-date=June 22, 2024 |publisher=Supreme Court E-Library}} Following the creation of Southern Leyte in 1959, these areas were moved to the [[Leyte's 4th congressional district|fourth district]], with the central municipalities from the fifth district, such as [[Alangalang, Leyte|Alangalang]], Barugo, Burauen, Capoocan, Carigara, Dagami, Jaro, Julita, La Paz, [[Pastrana, Leyte|Pastrana]], Tabontabon, and Tunga, forming the redefined second district from 1961 until its second dissolution in 1972.{{cite PH act|chamber=RA|number=2227|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra1959/ra_2227_1959.html |title=An Act Creating the Province of Southern Leyte|date=May 22, 1959 |publisher=The Lawphil Project - Arellano Law Foundation, Inc. |accessdate=6 May 2020}} ==Representation history== {| class=wikitable |- ! rowspan="2" | # ! rowspan="2" colspan=2 | Image ! rowspan="2" | Member ! colspan=2 | Term of office ! rowspan="2" | Legislature ! rowspan="2" | Party ! rowspan="2" | Electoral history ! rowspan="2" | Constituent
